content.text:
<context query="human-oversight gate stopped wrapping each tool executor" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="docs/human-oversight.md" type="doc" relevance="0.99" tokens="463">
## Where it is enforced

1. **Definition time.** `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts:60-66`, `enforceIdempotent`,
   throws when a TMS tool is defined with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. It covers
   only tools built through that factory.
2. **Call time.** `apps/api/src/oversight/oversightHooks.ts:29`, the
   `requires_human_action` branch of the `oversight` fragment on HAL Engine's
   `beforeToolCall` hook, returns the declined result, and the engine then never calls
   the executor. The hook fires before every call to a registered tool, whichever file
   registered it. `supportAgentHooks` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` installs the fragment
   first in the one `composeHooks([...])` array, as a `firstOrFail` chain: a fragment
   can decline or abstain, never allow, and if the policy itself throws, the engine
   declines the call instead of running it.

Two backstops keep the table honest. `assertAllToolsDeclared`, called from
`apps/api/src/server.ts` before the port opens, refuses to start the api while a
registered tool has no row, and names the tool. A test fails when any table row other
than the fixture is not `read_only`, so the first write tool cannot merge before
approve-then-execute (#47) lands.

Until `@re-cinq/hal-engine` 0.3.0 the gate wrapped each executor at registration,
because no hook fired around a tool call. Since 0.3.0 it runs on `beforeToolCall`
(#193); the table and the declined result carried over unchanged, and the wrapper is
gone. `apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts` stays the only file under `apps/api/src/`
that may call `.register(`, and a CI step fails any other. The one wrapper it still
applies is the crash guard (#185), which declines nothing: it turns an executor's throw
into one `tool_crash` audit row and one `tool_crashed` escalation. It has no
customer-scope resolver yet; #18 adds it.
</document>
<document source="specs/support-agent-human-oversight/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.96" tokens="1892">
## Reconciled Decisions

- **RD-01 - Where the hook kinds live. Settled.** #50's criteria place `composeHooks` in `apps/api/src/hooks/composeHooks.ts` and the exhaustiveness fixture in `exhaustiveness.ts`, and declare `HOOK_KINDS` without naming its file. Both later issues name the split: #151 registers its kind in "`apps/api/src/hooks/hookKinds.ts` and `composeHooks.ts`", and #193 adds "a `firstOrFail` `HookKind` to `apps/api/src/hooks/hookKinds.ts` and `composeHooks.ts`". FR-021 therefore puts `HookKind` and `HOOK_KINDS` in `hookKinds.ts` and the chain implementations in `composeHooks.ts`.
- **RD-02 - Two chain kinds or four. Settled.** #50 defines `thread` and `all`, says "every other point is an `all` chain", and types "all seven points". #151 adds `firstOrSkip` for `onToolBudgetExhausted` and #193 adds `firstOrFail` for `beforeToolCall`, each against a bumped engine, which is exactly the arrival #50's exhaustive map was built to force. FR-023 and FR-024 state the result, with each new row tied to the engine release that brings its hook. Superseded: #50's "every other point" and "all seven points" as fixed statements.
- **RD-03 - Where the gate sits. Settled.** #33 wraps every executor at the registration site because no hook fired around a tool call; #50 keeps "`063`'s per-executor wrapper" out of the composer, "enforced at registration"; #47 leaves it "unchanged here" and says it "migrates onto it later"; #151 lists installing `beforeToolCall` through the composer as out of scope, "declined by" #47. #193 is that migration: it deletes the wrapper, states the wrapper criterion is replaced and must not be restored, and keeps the authority table, the startup check and the definition-time refusal as backstops. FR-009 and FR-010 state it as before and after the engine pin; the pin is `@re-cinq/hal-engine` 0.3.0, so FR-010 holds. Superseded: #33 FR-003 and FR-004 (after the pin), #50's and #151's out-of-scope lines.
- **RD-04 - Is `needs_manual_tms_check` an escalation trigger. Open.** #47 requires a timed-out authorised write to produce "a `needs_manual_tms_check` escalation record" without saying whether it is a new `EscalationTrigger` member, and the executor runs on the authorisation path, outside a customer turn and its `afterSession` flush. See [support-agent-escalation](../support-agent-escalation/spec.md) RD-01 and RD-02, where the trigger union and its count are also open. FR-058 keeps #47's wording.
- **RD-05 - A third `ToolAuthority` member. Settled.** #33 makes a third value fail `npm run typecheck` and requires every production tool to be `read_only`. #47 explicitly gives `ToolAuthority` a third member, `records_intent`, and says #33's test becomes "every production tool is `read_only` or `records_intent`". #47 is conditional on `KU-20`, so FR-001 and FR-005 add the member once authorised actions are built. Superseded in part: #33 FR-013's `read_only`-only test.
- **RD-06 - The enforcement points in `docs/human-oversight.md`. Settled.** #33 requires "the two enforcement points by file and line". #193 requires the document to "name the two enforcement points as they now are, the definition-time refusal and this fragment, by file". CR-001 names them per stage; #47's section (CR-013) keeps its own "two enforcement points, by file and line" wording, which #47 does not spell out.
- **RD-07 - Blocked-result fixtures. Settled.** #33 tests the constant result with `note: 'Ole Larsen'`, #193 with `note: 'customer note text'`. The claims are the same; CR-006 and CR-007 keep both fixture values.
- **RD-08 - Which budget a blocked call consumes. Open.** #33 records that a blocked call still consumes the tool budget, citing `brief.md` PA-12 and `MAX_TOOL_CALLS` 5, the name `CLAUDE.md` uses. `support-agent-tms-tool-contract` (#19) and #151 name the setting `MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` / `maxToolRounds`. See [support-agent-escalation](../support-agent-escalation/spec.md) RD-05.
- **RD-09 - Approve-then-execute. Settled.** #33 puts it out of scope, "queued conditionally" on `KU-20`. #47 is that issue and stays conditional on `KU-20`, so FR-040 to FR-062 are headed as conditional.
- **RD-10 - Where `oversight` sits in the array. Settled as built.** #193's criterion installs the fragment "first in the `beforeToolCall` order within the single `composeHooks([...])` array", while its body says "first in the single `composeHooks([...])` array". #50 fixes persistence, audit, escalation, and #151 places `budget` fourth. Because `oversight` claims only `beforeToolCall`, both readings keep persistence ahead of audit and escalation. As built, `oversight` is first in the whole array, which satisfies both readings (FR-012).
- **RD-11 - The path #193's success criterion names. Settled.** #193 asks for `specs/support-agent-before-tool-call-oversight/spec.md` to exist with a validated-by link on every testable statement. The per-ticket spec is merged into this feature spec, so SC-004 names this file and scopes the links to #193's statements.
- **RD-12 - The tool crash wrapper and `withHumanOversight`. Settled in the TMS tools feature.** `support-agent-tool-crash-wrapper` (#185), in [support-agent-tms-tools](../support-agent-tms-tools/spec.md), composes its guard around `withHumanOversight`, which FR-010 has deleted. That spec's FR-066 and RD-4 state the composition after #193: `withCrashGuard(name, executor)`, with oversight on `beforeToolCall`.
- **RD-13 - The logger drops the composer's failure fields. Settled.** #50 adds `fragment`, `hook` and `fragments` to `SAFE_STRING_KEYS`, because all three carry names chosen in code, never customer text; the redaction test stays. CR-011 requires the failure line to carry `fragment`, `hook` and `sessionId`. `apps/api/src/shared/logger.ts` drops any string outside its allowlist (`event`, `sessionId`, `userId`, `orgId`, `code`, `status`, `reason`), so `fragment` and `hook` never reach a sink as written, and `CLAUDE.md` requires the redaction test to stay. The same applies to the startup lines in FR-013 and FR-036 unless they travel in the event name. See [support-agent-escalation](../support-agent-escalation/spec.md) RD-06.

## Issue Map

| Issue | Title                                                                     | Contributes                                                                                                 | State                               |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| #33   | Enforce human oversight over every consequential tool call                | `ToolAuthority`, authority table, deny by default, startup check, blocked result, `docs/human-oversight.md` | Open                                |
| #47   | Perform a consequential action only after a named OLT human authorises it | Approve-then-execute: action catalogue, `request_authorised_action`, executor, write key, `records_intent`  | Blocked: KU-20 (conditional), KU-02 |
| #50   | Compose the support agent's orchestrator hook fragments into one object   | `composeHooks`, `thread` and `all` chains, exhaustive `HOOK_KINDS`, single-registration grep                | Open                                |
| #193  | Run the oversight gate on the engine's beforeToolCall hook, fail closed   | `firstOrFail` chain, `oversightHooks.ts`, removal of the per-executor wrapper                               | Open                                |
</document>
</section>
<section name="Relevant Code" source="code" priority="2">
<document source="apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts" type="code" relevance="0.94" tokens="85">

From 0.3.0 it runs on the engine's `beforeToolCall` hook as the `oversight` fragment in `apps/api/src/hooks/oversightHooks.ts`. #193 deleted the wrapper, and the authority table and declined result carried over unchanged. I could not find a calendar date for the change, only the engine version and issue number.
